### III. 14. 6-11.] MAHÂVAGGA. 155

<meta>continues from previous page: the monk departed</meta>
...he returns within those seven days. In that case, O monks, the monk's earlier retreat <note>the vassa entering at the earlier date</note> is recognized, and there is no offense regarding his promise. ||6||

In another case... he departs on business when the <term>Pavāraṇā</term> <gloss>ceremony marking the end of the rainy retreat</gloss> is seven days away. Whether that monk returns to that residence or not, O monks, the monk's earlier retreat is recognized, and there is no offense regarding his promise. ||7||

In this case, O monks, a monk has promised to enter the rainy season retreat at the earlier time. Having gone to that residence, he performs the <term>Uposatha</term> <gloss>observance day ceremony</gloss>, enters the monastery on the day after the full moon <note>the first day of the following lunar fortnight</note>, prepares his seat, provides drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the courtyard. That very day, he departs without any urgent business. In that case, O monks, the monk's earlier retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of <term>dukkaṭa</term> <gloss>wrongdoing</gloss> regarding his promise. ||8||

In another case... <note>as in section 8</note>... he departs that very day on business... [etc.] ...having lived there for two or three days, he departs without urgent business... [etc.] ...having lived there for two or three days, he departs on business... [etc.] ...having lived there for two or three days, he departs for business that can be completed in seven days. He spends those seven days outside. In that case, O monks, the monk's earlier retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of wrongdoing regarding his promise. ||9||

Having lived there for two or three days, he departs for business that can be completed in seven days. He returns within those seven days. In that case, O monks, the monk's earlier retreat is recognized, and there is no offense regarding his promise. If seven days remain <note>until the ceremony</note>... <note>as in section 7</note>... there is no offense. ||10||

In this case, O monks, a monk has promised to enter the rainy season retreat at the later time. While going to that residence, he performs the <term>Uposatha</term> outside, enters the monastery on the day after the full moon, prepares his seat, provides drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the courtyard. That very day, he departs without any urgent business. In that case, O monks, the monk's later retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of wrongdoing regarding his promise. In another case... <note>the entire following passage is identical with sections 5 through 10; however, read "later" and "for the later retreat" instead of "earlier" and "for the earlier retreat," and read "before the Komudī full moon of the fourth month" instead of "before the Pavāraṇā ceremony"</note>... and there is no offense regarding his promise. ||11||14||

The third chapter, on entering the rainy season retreat, is concluded.

The summary of its contents:
Entering, when, and how many, during the rains,
Not wishing, intentionally, to postpone, and the lay follower.

<summary>This page concludes the legal rulings on entering the rainy season retreat (Vassa), detailing the conditions under which a monk's retreat is considered valid or invalid if he departs from his residence. It provides specific exemptions for business that can be concluded within seven days and distinguishes between the earlier and later retreat periods.</summary>
